title: B-2 uses Biefield-Brown effect
summary: Jesse Michels tells of B-2 uses Biefield-Brown effect, about 1992 at United States (no place named), and reports it citing named sources. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: In March of 1992, Aviation Week broke a story about the B-2 stealth bomber.

intentionally created a lot of
disinformation about his work to protect
it he showed people his fluid dialectric
system that used ionic wind instead of
the solid dialectric gravitator we now
even know that the B2 stealth bomber
uses Brown's Electric gravitics
tellings.difference: This telling credits Paul Schatzkin's The Man Who Mastered Gravity rather than Aviation Week, gives no date, and frames the B-2 claim with Brown's deliberate disinformation: he showed people an ionic-wind fluid-dielectric system instead of the solid-dielectric gravitator.
tellings.link_reason: Both have Jesse Michels claiming that the B-2 stealth bomber uses Townsend Brown's electrogravitics (the Biefeld-Brown effect). The telling's 'we now even know' points to the same claim the story attributes to the 1992 Aviation Week report.

as_told.title: Brown's deliberate disinformation and electrogravitics in the B-2 bomber

tellings.quote: I'm convinced his work made it into the B2 stealth bomber this like Premier you know stealth bomber you know and he was he was paid off by this Finance here at North Grumman like a ridiculously low sum of money for the rest of his life
tellings.difference: Adds that Northrop Grumman paid Brown off with a very small sum for the rest of his life, mentions Catalina Island, and rests on the host's conviction rather than the Aviation Week report.
tellings.link_reason: Both claim that Townsend Brown's electrogravitic work made it into the B-2 stealth bomber built by Northrop.

as_told.title: Townsend Brown's work in the B-2 and payoff by Northrop Grumman

tellings.quote: We have a lot of evidence that his electro-hydrodnamics work, you know, this electric fields to manipulate airflow work ended up in the B2 stealth bomber.
tellings.difference: Frames it as electrohydrodynamic airflow control and says 'a lot of evidence' without naming the Aviation Week source.
tellings.link_reason: Same claim that Brown's electric-field work ended up in the B-2 stealth bomber.

as_told.title: Brown's electrohydrodynamics work in the B-2 stealth bomber
